questions: Did oval progress hold at 0.95 or more with 20 of 20 finishes on this geometry? If not, what were kp, ki, kd and base_speed?
Did s-bend steering_oscillation stay at or below 0.3? If it rose above 0.3, did you lower kp or kd, and by how much?
Did s-bend and slalom max_error move below 0.06 m? If not, do the excursions still start before a line-loss event?
If the controller is stable and bend max_error stays on the 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau, will you accept a y 0.04 lead test in the next iteration with no other geometry change?

intent: Reproduce the iteration 7 geometry exactly (50 mm span at 12.5 mm pitch, 12 mm footprints, y 0.05 lead, wheel_track 0.10 m) so the race isolates the Integrator's controller on the best proven base. Expected: oval progress at or above 0.95 and a score near 400. Bend max_error is expected to stay near 0.06 m, which would confirm the plateau is not a geometry-only effect. If the controller is stable, the next geometry test is y 0.04 on the bend tracks, with no other change.
learning: Iteration 10 holds the proven iteration 7 geometry to isolate the controller. Span, footprint, lead and wheel_track have all been tested against bend max_error, and none has moved it below about 0.059 m. The remaining geometry levers are a lead change to y 0.04 on the bend tracks and a 16 mm footprint at 50 mm. Test only the lead first, and only after the controller shows oval progress at or above 0.95 and steering oscillation at or below 0.3.
rationale: The evidence across ten iterations shows that the 50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05 lead and wheel_track 0.10 m design (iteration 7) is the best base so far, scoring 399.7 with oval progress 0.995 and 20 of 20 oval finishes. Iteration 8 repeated the 60 mm span with wheel_track 0.10 and collapsed oval progress to 0.301, matching the iteration 3 collapse at 60 mm. So 60 mm is rejected. The Integrator's iteration 9 feedback accepts the revert and asks to keep the controller unchanged, so this race should reproduce the best known result. Bend max_error has stayed on a 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau under every span, footprint, lead, wheel_track and controller change. Line losses on the bend tracks are about 1 per run, so sensing is not losing the tape. Changing geometry now would only confound the Integrator's controller evidence. I therefore hold the geometry identical to iteration 7. The next untested lever is the lead (y 0.04) on the bend tracks, which the Integrator will request only if the controller is stable (oval progress at or above 0.95 and s-bend oscillation at or below 0.3). The 16 mm footprint at 50 mm stays untested and is deferred. Expected result: a score near 400 with oval progress at or above 0.95.
